sources.entry: pandas - A library providing high-performance, easy-to-use data structures and data analysis tools.

summary.one_liner: pandas is a Python data analysis library providing labeled data structures (Series and DataFrame) and tools for cleaning, reshaping, merging, grouping, and time series work.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes pandas as a Python package offering fast, flexible data structures for relational or labeled data. Listed features include handling of missing data (NaN, NA, NaT), inserting and deleting columns, automatic label-based data alignment, split-apply-combine group-by operations, and reshaping and pivoting. It also covers label-based slicing and subsetting, merging and joining, hierarchical (multi-level) axis labels, and I/O for CSV and delimited files, Excel, databases, and HDF5. Time series support includes date range generation, frequency conversion, moving-window statistics, and date shifting. The README links to full documentation hosted on pandas.pydata.org.
use_cases: clean and handle missing values in tabular data
load and save CSV, Excel, database, or HDF5 data
time series resampling and rolling statistics
notable: Series and DataFrame labeled data structures with automatic data alignment
Built-in I/O for flat files, Excel, databases, and HDF5
Time series date range generation, frequency conversion, and rolling windows
caveats: tzdata is only required on Windows and Emscripten according to the README
Full installation requirements and minimum supported versions are defined in external docs, not the README
Installation from source is documented separately
